author: Cad82
title: Beautifully designed, but systematically frustrating.
content: The graphics and animations in Royal Kingdom are undeniably top-notch, and the experience is entirely free of intrusive third-party ads. However, the game replaces traditional ads with aggressive in-game promotions for upgrade packs, to the point where I would actually prefer the option to watch ads if it meant I could voluntarily farm coins or upgrades. Instead, you are starved of resources, making it nearly impossible to collect enough coins through normal gameplay to keep things fun. Winning relies far more on the luck of how gems fall and boosters align than actual skill, and this luck feels artificially manipulated to entice you into spending money. The move limits seem systematically engineered to leave you exactly one or two moves away from winning, dangling purchasable coin packs in your face precisely when your frustration peaks. To make matters worse, you cannot replay past levels to farm coins, and running out of lives forces you into absurdly long wait times unless you pay real money to keep playing. I do not mind paying for a fun experience, but gone are the days of a fair, one-time purchase price for unlimited gameplay. While technically free-to-play, Royal Kingdom seems systematically designed to be a frustration engine that punishes you for not spending real money. I will be moving on to games that either offer voluntary ad-farming options or respect the player with a traditional, one-time purchase model.
